question: A 29-year-old woman comes to the physician because of intermittent episodes of sharp chest pain and palpitations. She appears nervous. Her pulse is 115/min and irregularly irregular, and blood pressure is 139/86 mmHg. Examination shows a fine tremor on both hands and digital swelling; the extremities are warm. There is retraction of the right upper eyelid. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in the management of this patient?
analysis: The patient is presenting with signs and symptoms suggestive of hyperthyroidism, specifically Graves' disease, given the presence of tremors, digital swelling, warm extremities, and retraction of the right upper eyelid (lid lag). The irregularly irregular pulse is indicative of atrial fibrillation, a common complication of untreated hyperthyroidism. The most appropriate next step in the management of this patient would be to start beta-blocker therapy to control her symptoms and heart rate. Propranolol is a non-selective beta-blocker that can help with symptom control in hyperthyroidism.
